equality.method: driver.run_game with observer (every decide output JSON) + post (events_json + md5 of board_json after every applied move), sort_keys JSONL; mainline = worktree @ dadd89e with its own wheel, merged = this branch with its wheel; compared line by line

latency_1core.how: taskset -c N (4 runs side by side on cores 0-3, one per core; 4 worlds share one core), rs_decide_latency.py --budget 0 --games 8, same seeds

notes: Invariant held: every decide output, every applied move's events and the board after it are identical to mainline on 2,826 decision points (3 settings). Goldens were not regenerated and are green.

Nothing from either speed branch was dropped as an effect: where both did the same thing (in-place on-play probe with journaled DonPush, rel zero-fill skip, single pending read in drains) one implementation was kept; where they differed only in hashing, A's Fx hasher was used crate-wide (one hasher, lookup-only tables) and B's FNV was removed; ProfileCache uses B's dense index (faster than any hash map).

Combined speedup (wall, 1 core): 1x1280 x2.00, 4x1280 x1.87, 1x5120 x2.00 — larger than either branch alone (A x1.50 / B x1.39 at 1x1280), as expected since A mostly cut forward/encode repeats and B cut JSON building/copies.

Latency runs were 4 concurrent single-core-pinned processes (mainline and merged at the same time on separate cores), so absolute numbers include shared-cache/memory-bandwidth effects; the ratio is what to read. Mainline 1x1280 (279 s) matches rs-speed-a's own 'before' (284 s).

Rethink (play-rethink) is default off; with off, driver.run_game goes through engine.decide_with_rethink which returns the single decide unchanged — confirmed by the equality dump above (which ran through that path on the merged side) and tests/test_play_rethink.py.
The equality/compare scripts were work-only (scratchpad), not committed, per §7.2.
Python deps (fastapi etc. from opcg_sim/requirements.txt, pytest-xdist, maturin) had to be installed in this fresh container before the gates.
